title: Document the gh run rerun recovery for stuck idd-advisory-convergence rollups; investigate concurrency hardening
body:
## Background

`idd-advisory-convergence` (added by #1341/#1345 to close roadmap
#1342) is a required status check that asserts Copilot's review has
converged on a PR's current HEAD. During a single autonomous-loop
session on 2026-07-15, at least eight independent PRs
(#1366/#1374/#1368/#1370/#1373/#1371/#1367/#1376/#1375/#1378/#1372/#1369
— issues #1358, #1359, #1360, #1361, #1362, #1363, #1364, #1365,
#1350, #1351, #1355, #1356) hit the same recovery problem before
merging, each rediscovering it independently:

1. **`workflow_dispatch` does not refresh the PR's required-check
   rollup.** Even when the dispatch input (`pr_number`) targets the
   right PR and the run's own `--assert` evaluates the right PR content
   via the GitHub API, the resulting check-run does not update the
   PR's `statusCheckRollup` / required-check evaluation for its HEAD
   SHA — the rollup stays pinned to the stale FAILURE/CANCELLED run.
   This directly contradicts the workflow file's own header comment
   (`.github/workflows/idd-advisory-convergence.yml`, "workflow_dispatch
   (manual re-run)" section), which frames `workflow_dispatch` as "a
   one-click affordance" for exactly this re-check scenario.
2. **The only reliable recovery every agent converged on** was
   `gh run rerun <existing-run-id>` (re-running the *same* check-run
   object tied to the PR's HEAD SHA) rather than dispatching a new run.
   This is not documented anywhere in the workflow file or the
   `idd-advisory-wait`/`idd-ci` instruction surfaces — each agent had
   to rediscover it empirically from the Checks API.
3. **Contributing factor**: the workflow's `cancel-in-progress: true`
   concurrency group (keyed by PR number) sometimes cancels a
   legitimately in-flight run when a near-simultaneous review event
   (Copilot/CodeRabbit/Codex posting review comments in quick
   succession) fires another trigger for the same PR. The resulting
   stale `CANCELLED` entry can then race a later genuine `SUCCESS` in
   the rollup display. This is worse under heavy concurrent-session
   load — the normal operating condition for this repository — because
   many PRs' review threads tend to land close together.

No PR in this session ever merged with a genuinely-failing check; the
friction was entirely in getting GitHub's required-check rollup
display to reflect state that was already true. This is a process/CI
reliability gap, not a correctness or security bug in the convergence
verdict logic itself.

## Proposed change

1. **Document the working recovery procedure** directly in
   `.github/workflows/idd-advisory-convergence.yml`'s existing
   "workflow_dispatch (manual re-run)" header-comment section (and its
   `idd-template/` mirror if one exists), stating plainly that
   `workflow_dispatch` does not reliably flip the PR's required-check
   rollup and that `gh run rerun <run-id>` on the existing PR-linked
   run (found via `gh run list --workflow=idd-advisory-convergence.yml
   ...` or the Checks API) is the verified recovery path. Cross-link
   this from `idd-advisory-wait.instructions.md` and/or
   `idd-ci.instructions.md` wherever they currently point agents at
   `workflow_dispatch` for this check, so a future agent does not have
   to rediscover this empirically.
2. **Investigate whether the trigger/concurrency-group design can be
   hardened** so a stale `CANCELLED`/`FAILURE` run stops racing out a
   later genuine `SUCCESS` in the rollup under rapid review-event
   bursts — for example, a narrower `cancel-in-progress` scope, a
   revised concurrency group key, or a trigger-condition adjustment.
   This workflow's existing header comments show its trigger/checkout
   topology was already deliberately and carefully reasoned about
   (tamper-resistant default-branch checkout, event coverage
   trade-offs) — any change here must preserve that reasoning, not
   just chase this symptom.
   - If a low-risk change is identified that doesn't weaken the
     tamper-resistance or event-coverage properties documented in the
     existing header comments, implement it and validate with the
     repository's normal `lint`/`idd-doctor` checks, explaining the
     change in a header-comment addition consistent with this file's
     existing extensively-commented style.
   - If no safe mechanical fix is identified (i.e. the race is an
     inherent property of GitHub Actions' check-run/rollup model that
     this repository cannot control from the workflow side), record
     that investigation finding directly in the same header-comment
     section instead, so a future reader does not re-investigate the
     same dead end.

## Acceptance criteria

- `.github/workflows/idd-advisory-convergence.yml`'s header comment
  documents the verified `gh run rerun <run-id>` recovery procedure for
  a stuck/stale required-check rollup, explicitly correcting the
  existing claim that `workflow_dispatch` is a sufficient one-click
  re-trigger for this scenario.
- `idd-advisory-wait.instructions.md` and/or `idd-ci.instructions.md`
  (wherever they currently reference `workflow_dispatch` for this
  check) are updated to point agents at the verified recovery
  procedure instead.
- The concurrency/trigger investigation concludes in one of two
  objectively-checkable ways, recorded in the workflow file's own
  header comment: (a) a low-risk hardening change is implemented and
  the repository's `lint`/`idd-doctor` checks pass, or (b) the
  investigation finding ("no safe mechanical fix identified, and why")
  is documented in place of a code change.
- No change weakens the trusted-default-branch-checkout tamper
  resistance or the documented event-coverage rationale already in the
  workflow file.

Refs #1341 #1345 #1342
